# Issue 3863 -- "Support -H and -P at the same time"
#
# GRAMMAR WARNING. Do not read a generic `bisect` result as this issue's
# release history. dxc's preprocess option changed grammar at 8bf2b087c
# (PR 4624, 2022-08-31): before it, `P : Separate<["-","/"],"P">`, so
# `-P <name>` names the OUTPUT file and `-Fi` does not exist. Releases up to
# v1.7.2207 answer `Unknown argument: '-Fi'` for line 2 below, and the
# `/Fi` spelling retry that provokes turns line 2 into
# `-P repro.hlsl /Fi preprocessed.i -H`, i.e. "preprocess preprocessed.i into
# repro.hlsl" -- which overwrites the repro at exit 0. The runner now isolates
# every attempt and hard-fails input mutation, so the committed evidence is
# safe, but no single command line spans both eras. Release history therefore
# comes from manual-case-release-history.txt, which uses the spelling each
# release accepts and visits every stable release (a linear scan).
#
# 1: CONTROL, and it runs inside every probe rather than beside it. `-H` on an
#    ordinary compile must print `Opening file [...]` for inc-comp-a.h. This is
#    match.json's self-test: it proves the instrument is alive in this very run,
#    so the absence measured on line 2 cannot be a dead search.
# 2: THE REPRO. `-P` plus `-H`, with `-H` last so it sits where the option under
#    test goes.
# 3: `dxc -P` writes only to a file, so nothing it produced would reach a
#    predicate. Compiling the generated .i with -Zi embeds that text in
#    !dx.source.contents, which puts the preprocessed output -- header bodies
#    included -- onto stdout where match.json can require it. That is the
#    positive anchor proving line 2 really preprocessed and really opened both
#    headers.
-T ps_6_0 -E main -H control-compile.hlsl
-P repro.hlsl -Fi preprocessed.i -H
-T ps_6_0 -E main -Zi preprocessed.i
